event: The party descends south through the Tower, and the stone's signal does not change.
Solenne files it: the Tower does not track which way they walk.
At Floor 29 Tomás stops at the threshold marking he already has indexed.
He studies it nine seconds, makes a notation and walks on.
Solenne does not ask; she files his signal under later.
In the first hour of descent, Dayo comes to walk beside Miriam.
Solenne reads Dayo's Steadfast signal: the same weight, now held at two points.
Miriam asks about the chokepoint geometry on Floor 27; Dayo answers.
Miriam's Warmhearted signal is not clinical now, just here.
Solenne files that the catalog needs a new entry.
Six days of descent: the rest nodes are familiar going south.
Solenne knows the best wall in the Floor 26 node for her Conductor readings.
The cleared floors stay cleared: no enemies respawn on the way down.
On Floor 23 Vesper runs the Workframe at junctions: still Section 11-30 material.
At the Floor 22 rest node she tells Tomás it is the same section all the way.
Tomás says expected; Vesper says worth confirming.
On Floor 21, the party rounds the east corridor's third-section bend.
They walk in loose traveling formation, Tomás's Eagle Eye at half-extension.
Nadia stops, going still before her attention sharpens.
She says flatly: it's been running.
At the corridor's end stands the door with the Composite designation.
Vesper reads the door with the Workframe at full reach: same hand.
She says it is built for threshold crossing, its load path through the party.
It was expecting use, she tells Solenne.
Tomás finds an inlaid marking in the unknown script below the Composite symbol.
Eight characters: four in his index, two he lacks; he records it.
Solenne runs the Conductor on the door: the six frequencies, like a tuned instrument.
Solenne says ready.
Dayo says Six of Six; Solenne confirms.
Solenne holds all six signals in sustained deep contact.
Steadfast, Warmhearted, Clearvoiced, Openhanded, Brightspirit, Trueweave, each itself.
She activates, and the door's frequencies shift like a chord resolving.
The door opens without sound or System notice; the lock reads resolved.
Tomás enters first, notation surface ready.
The room is shaped like a study, with three walls of stone shelving.
The shelves hold folded documents in an unknown material.
On the central shelf lies a dark stone panel carved with characters in columns.
Tomás sets his notation surface on the floor and stands with his hands at his sides.
He picks up the panel and counts sixty-eight characters, split by separators.
He sets it down and documents for four minutes without speaking.
Miriam holds her notebook closed; Vesper inventories the shelves; Dayo stands by the door.
Tomás says he has enough for the first sequence, though not the full key.
A notice in the Tower's own voice appears, visible only inside the room.
Miriam reads it aloud: the party that opens this room is the one the Tower built toward.
The panel is the Tower's own record of the Architect language, incomplete.
The rest lies in Repository Nodes on Floors 17, 32 and 48.
Tomás says Floor 17 is four floors down, in the Apex corridor: they'd need Cassia.
Dayo checks her time display: one day four hours; Floor 17 is out of reach.
Dayo asks if he can read the first sequence; after four seconds he says yes.
Tomás reads it aloud, and the party is quiet.
Miriam writes fast in her notebook's main text; Nadia looks at Dayo.
Dayo says they come back for Floor 17 when they have the window.
She tells Tomás to take everything he can carry; he packs the documentation.
They leave the room before the evening shift; the door seals behind them.
Dayo checks the time: one day. She calls formation, north toward the rest node.
The first sequence is five words: The mechanism works because you chose.
Solenne reads it as past tense: the Tower designed it, they made it work.
At the junction she reads a new register in Dayo's Steadfast signal.
She files it under the work.
